title: U.S. Bombers Leave a British Air Base After a Security Scare
summary:
The U.S. Air Force has brought its bombers home from RAF Fairford, a U.S.-run military air base in England, the Associated Press reports. The move follows a British investigation into a suspected plan to attack the base.

RAF Fairford is about 100 miles (160 kilometers) west of London. American bombers have used it during decades of conflicts in the Middle East. Since the start of the U.S. war with Iran, aviation watchers have seen dozens of large B-52 and B-1 bombers operating from the base. On Sunday, observers noticed many B-1 bombers flying out of Fairford.

In late September, police responded to a security incident at the base. Last week, a man who holds both British and Iranian citizenship was arrested in London on suspicion of planning a terror attack. In total, six people were taken into custody during the investigation and later released on bail, which means they were allowed to leave custody while the investigation continues. British officials have linked the incident to Iran's government. Iran has denied that it was involved.

The bombers' departure comes as President Donald Trump weighs his next steps in the conflict with Iran, including the possibility of new strikes. When the campaign began, he had told Americans it would last only a matter of weeks.

The U.S. military still has a large presence in the Middle East. A U.S. official said the aircraft carrier USS Theodore Roosevelt and a group of ships carrying more than 7,000 sailors and 2,000 Marines are heading to the region. The official said that could mean three U.S. aircraft carriers in the area as early as the end of October.
why_it_matters: The move shows how a security threat can change U.S. military plans abroad during an ongoing conflict with Iran.
